Done. Nothing committed or pushed, per the working agreement.

## Root cause — confirmed, not inferred

I pulled the artifacts from run 34127634577 rather than re-deriving. The droid `entire.log` on Windows contains **only git hooks**:

```
prepare-commit-msg (git) ×2   commit-msg (git) ×2   post-commit (git) ×2
prepare-commit-msg: no active sessions
```

Zero agent hooks. Same run, same runner, claude-code has `session-start/user-prompt-submit/stop/session-end` ×2 each and passes. So no droid hook ever fires; there is no session, so the commit has nothing to condense.

**It is not the `sh` wrapper being unsupported** — claude-code uses byte-identical `sh -c '…'` wrappers and passes on that runner. It is *who runs them*. I read droid's own hook-spawn code out of the shipped binaries:

| droid build | hook spawn |
|---|---|
| darwin 0.215.1 | `{command, shell: "sh"}` |
| windows 0.109.1 | `spawn("cmd.exe", ["/c", H])` |
| windows 0.178.0 | `{command, shell: "cmd.exe"}` |
| windows 0.215.1 | `spawn(%ComSpec%, ["/d","/s","/c",H], {windowsVerbatimArguments:true})` |

**Every Windows droid build hands the hook command to cmd.exe**; only the non-Windows build uses `sh`. cmd.exe reads our wrapper's `>/dev/null` and `2>&1` as its own redirections and `&` as a separator, so the line is shredded and `entire` is never executed. Silently — droid logs hook failures only to its own log.

## Why the existing shared helper wasn't enough

`agent.UseWindowsProductionHooks` is probe-gated: it swaps in the cmd.exe wrappers only when `sh -c 'exit 0'` fails. That probe command contains **no cmd.exe metacharacters**, so on a GitHub runner (Git Bash present) it reports success — and droid would have kept the sh wrapper and stayed broken. Codex and Cursor legitimately keep the probe; they resolve a shell themselves, so a working sh really does mean the sh wrapper runs.

## The change (4 files, +221/−9)

- `agent/hook_command.go` — new `HookHostIsWindows()` (plain host check over the existing `hookCommandOS` test seam) and `WrapProductionPlainTextWarningHookCommandForOS`, the missing selector for the one wrapper shape droid uses that had no `…ForOS` variant.
- `agent/factoryaidroid/hooks.go` — all seven commands go through the `…ForOS` selectors gated on `HookHostIsWindows()`, with a comment saying why droid does *not* use the probe.
- Tests in both packages.

Migration is free: `dropStaleEntireHooks` already replaces any managed hook not in the wanted set, and `IsManagedHookCommand` recognises both Windows wrapper shapes — I added an assertion pinning that, since it is what stops a repo ending up with both entries double-firing.

## Verification

- Both new droid tests **fail** with the probe-gated predicate and pass with `HookHostIsWindows()` — they specifically pin "a working sh on Windows must not keep the sh wrapper". They are named `…Windows…` so the `test-windows` CI job actually runs them on a real Windows runner.
- `mise run test:integration` (562 tests) and `mise run test:e2e:canary` (4/4) pass; lint clean.
- `mise run test` has 3 failures — all reproduce unchanged on pristine `origin/main`: two are the macOS `/var`→`/private/var` symlink tests, one is `TestRunUninstall_Codex…`, which passes once the orphan `entire-agent-devin/kilo/roger-roger` mise shims are off `$PATH`. None are mine.

## Two things I did not do

1. **No real Windows droid run.** The fix follows from droid's own code, but it is untested end-to-end; that needs a Windows box with `FACTORY_API_KEY` and paid API calls, so I'm asking before running `mise run test:e2e --agent factoryai-droid`. If there is a *second* Windows-specific defect behind this one, only that run will show it.
2. **Did not touch `nightly-e2e.yml`.** PR #2159 is still open, so per your instruction I'm flagging rather than editing: once it merges, restore `factoryai-droid` to the Windows `AGENTS` line plus `irm https://app.factory.ai/cli/windows | iex` and `~\bin` on `GITHUB_PATH` — the comment at line 170 of that file spells it out.

Branch is `fix-droid-ai-windows-test`, already based on current `origin/main` (not the nightly branch). Diff is uncommitted in the worktree for you to review.

ARM64 Windows build exists (`downloads.factory.ai/.../0.215.1/windows/arm64/droid.exe` → 200), so UTM on Apple Silicon is fine.

## Install droid

In PowerShell on the VM:

```powershell
irm https://app.factory.ai/cli/windows | iex
```

It auto-detects ARM64, verifies a SHA256, drops `droid.exe` in `%USERPROFILE%\bin`, and adds that to your **persistent** user PATH (open a new shell afterwards). Only prerequisite is `curl.exe`, built in since Win10 1803.

Auth, two options:
- **Factory login** — just run `droid` once, it opens a browser flow.
- **BYOK**, which is what our e2e uses and what you want for headless `droid exec`: put an `anthropic` entry in `%USERPROFILE%\.factory\settings.json` under `customModels` (same shape as `e2e/agents/droid.go:105`), then `droid exec --model custom:claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`.

## Before you spend an API call — the 30-second check

You can prove both the bug and the fix without droid running a single prompt, because the whole question is "what does cmd.exe do with this string". Set up an entire-enabled repo on the VM, then paste each wrapper **at a `cmd.exe` prompt** (the prompt *is* a cmd command line, so this is exactly the parse droid subjects it to):

Today's shipped form:
```
sh -c 'if ! command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then exit 0; fi; exec entire hooks factoryai-droid session-start'
```
This branch's Windows form:
```
cmd.exe /d /s /c "where.exe entire >nul 2>nul & if errorlevel 1 (ver>nul) else (entire hooks factoryai-droid session-start)"
```

Then `type .entire\logs\entire.log`. The first should leave **nothing** in the log (cmd eats `>/dev/null` as a redirection and the line dies before `entire` is reached) — that's the exact signature from the CI artifact. The second should log `session-start hook invoked`.

## The real end-to-end check

I cross-built the fixed CLI for you — `entire.exe` for Windows ARM64:

```
/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gtrrz-victor-wks-cli-uninstall-ext/b820186c-7396-45d5-9a5d-d8492b96fea1/scratchpad/entire-arm64.exe
```

Copy it into the VM, put it on PATH as `entire.exe`, then:

```
git init droidtest && cd droidtest
git commit --allow-empty -m init
entire enable --agent factoryai-droid
droid exec --skip-permissions-unsafe "create docs/red.md about the colour red, then git add and git commit it"
entire status
```

A checkpoint should appear. To see the failure first, install the *released* nightly `entire` instead and run the same thing — you'll get commits and no checkpoint.

Two things worth knowing before you start:
- **`entire enable` must run with the fixed binary.** The wrapper form is baked into `.factory/settings.json` at enable time, so re-enabling is what migrates a repo. A repo enabled by the old binary keeps the sh hook until the next install (the migration path is covered by `TestInstallHooks_WindowsMigratesShWrappers`).
- I have not run this myself — the fix follows from droid's own spawn code, but if a second Windows-specific defect is hiding behind this one, this run is what surfaces it.

If you'd rather I drive the full `mise run test:e2e --agent factoryai-droid TestMultiSessionSequential` on the VM instead, say so — that needs `FACTORY_API_KEY` + `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and makes real paid calls, which is why I'm not starting it unprompted.

input.message:
Please verify a Windows-only droid hook fix on branch fix-droid-ai-windows-test (commit ec586d9e5) — you have the branch and droid installed; I do not have a Windows box.

WHAT THE BUG IS — do not re-derive it, it is settled
factoryai-droid produced no checkpoint on Windows: commits land, not one agent hook fires. Proven from CI artifact run 34127634577: droid's entire.log contains only git hooks (prepare-commit-msg / commit-msg / post-commit) plus "prepare-commit-msg: no active sessions", while claude-code on the SAME runner with byte-identical `sh -c` wrappers fires session-start / user-prompt-submit / stop / session-end.

Cause: droid's WINDOWS build hands every hook command to cmd.exe (spawn("cmd.exe",["/c",H]) at 0.109.1, shell:"cmd.exe" at 0.178.0, %ComSpec% /d /s /c + windowsVerbatimArguments at 0.215.1); only its non-Windows build runs them under sh. cmd.exe reads our wrapper's `>/dev/null` and `2>&1` as its own redirections and `&` as a separator, so the line is shredded and `entire` is never executed. I read this out of the shipped droid binaries for all three versions, so treat it as established.

Fix: droid now installs the native cmd.exe wrappers whenever the host is Windows, via a new agent.HookHostIsWindows(). Deliberately NOT gated on agent.UseWindowsProductionHooks, whose probe only runs `sh -c 'exit 0'` — a command with no cmd.exe metacharacters — so a host with Git Bash reports "sh works" and would keep the broken sh wrapper.

WHAT I NEED FROM YOU

Step 0 — report your environment before doing anything else: `droid --version`, `go version`, whether mise is installed, `git log --oneline -1`, and whether FACTORY_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY are set (say set/unset, never print values).

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will process your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

Fix VERIFIED on real Windows. Step 1 passed exactly as you predicted; Step 2 impossible (both API keys unset); found one regression the fix left behind — 3 pre-existing droid unit tests now fail on Windows.

STEP 0 — ENVIRONMENT
droid 0.215.1 (so the version installed here is your %ComSpec% /d /s /c + windowsVerbatimArguments case)
go1.26.6 windows/arm64 — note ARM64
mise installed (scoop shim)
git log -1: ec586d9e5 factoryai-droid: install the cmd.exe hook wrappers on Windows
FACTORY_API_KEY: unset. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: unset.

Also relevant to your gating argument: `sh` IS on PATH here (Git Bash, scoop). So this box is exactly the host you designed HookHostIsWindows for — UseWindowsProductionHooks' `sh -c 'exit 0'` probe would have succeeded and kept the broken sh wrapper. Your choice not to gate on the probe is empirically justified on this machine.

STEP 1 — ALL AS PREDICTED
Built the branch, put it first on PATH (needed: three other entire.exe shadow it here, tools2 wins by machine PATH). Version string confirms ec586d9e5. Scratch repo + one empty commit + `entire enable --agent factoryai-droid` → "Installed 8 hooks".

.factory/settings.json: all 8 entries are cmd.exe forms, zero `sh -c '`. The fix took. Seven are `cmd.exe /d /s /c "where.exe entire >nul 2>nul & if errorlevel 1 (ver>nul) else (entire hooks ... )"`; the Stop entry is the bare (unprefixed) cmd form with the plain-text warning, as expected from its different wrapper shape.

(a) sh -c wrapper at a cmd command line, cwd=scratch repo:
    exit code 0, stderr "The system cannot find the path specified." (cmd trying to redirect to a file named /dev/null), and NO .entire\logs DIRECTORY CREATED AT ALL. entire never executed. That is the CI signature reproduced precisely — including the silent exit 0, which is why droid never reported anything wrong.

(b) native cmd.exe wrapper, same cwd:
    reached entire. Bare, it exits 1 with "failed to parse hook event: empty hook input" — i.e. it got all the way into hook dispatch and only lacked the stdin payload the real agent supplies. Fed a plausible payload ({"session_id":...,"transcript_path":...}) it exits 0, prints the context injection, and logs:
      "msg":"session-start","component":"lifecycle","agent":"factoryai-droid","event":"SessionStart","session_id":"win-verify-b"
    So (a) → nothing, (b) → a real session-start. Exactly your expectation.

Your Step 1(b) tests the stored string as a top-level command line, but droid hands that string to a shell, so the stored `cmd.exe /d /s /c "..."` gets nested inside droid's own `%ComSpec% /d /s /c`. I tested that, because if nesting broke, Step 1 would have looked fine and the e2e would still fail.

I could not test this through a .bat (the batch parser plus a `<` redirection on the same line produced a spurious `"" was unexpected at this time.` — disregard that if I'd reported it; it was my harness, not your code). I wrote a small Go spawner that sets SysProcAttr.CmdLine directly, reading the command line from a file so no shell requotes it — a byte-exact model of node's windowsVerbatimArguments. Both plausible compositions WORK, session-start logged for each:
  cmd.exe /d /s /c cmd.exe /d /s /c "where.exe entire >nul ..."   (0.215.1, args joined bare)  → exit 0, logged
  cmd.exe /d /s /c "cmd.exe /d /s /c "where.exe entire >nul ..."" (0.178.0, node shell: wraps) → exit 0, logged
cmd's /s "strip first and last quote" rule handles the nesting in both directions. So the fix is robust across the composition change between 0.178.0 and 0.215.1.

STEP 2 — CANNOT RUN
Both FACTORY_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY are unset in this session's environment, so `mise run test:e2e --agent factoryai-droid TestMultiSessionSequential` cannot make its calls. I did not attempt it and did not go looking for credentials elsewhere — that's the user's to supply. Everything above is free/no-API.

THE ONE PROBLEM — A REGRESSION YOUR COMMIT INTRODUCED
Running the full package suite on Windows, three PRE-EXISTING droid tests now fail on real assertions because they hardcode the OS-unaware wrapper while the implementation now installs cmd forms:
  TestInstallHooks_FreshInstall                  (8 assertions, all "X was not found", each quoting the sh -c command)
  TestInstallHooks_PreservesUserHooksOnSameType  (subtest PostToolUse; hooks_test.go:346/356/357/367)
  TestInstallHooks_ReplacesLegacyLocalDevHook    (hooks_test.go:112 "could not find the installed command ... to seed the legacy hook")
They call agentpkg.WrapProductionSilentHookCommand / WrapProductionPlainTextWarningHookCommand — the unconditional sh variants.

I verified this is genuinely yours and not the platform: I checked out main in a worktree and ran the same tests on this same box. On main every TestInstallHooks_* failure is "TempDir RemoveAll cleanup: ... being used by another process" with ZERO assertion failures. On your branch those three have real assertion failures. (For the avoidance of doubt: all the other FAILs I saw across ./cmd/entire/cli/agent/... — including the whole pi package and a pi absolute-path test — are pre-existing Windows harness artifacts, unrelated to you.)

Severity is moderate, not release-blocking, because CI will NOT catch it: ci.yml's windows-latest job runs `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/... -run '(Windows|MSYS)'`, and none of those three names match. Your two new tests DO match, and I confirmed the exact CI filter is green on both packages:
  go test ./cmd/entire/cli/agent ./cmd/entire/cli/agent/factoryaidroid -run '(Windows|MSYS)' -count=1  → ok, ok
So CI stays green, your new tests do run on the Windows runner as your commit message intends, but anyone running the full suite on Windows (your user, on this box) sees 3 red droid tests.

Fix shape, using what you already added: those three assertions want the ForOS selectors keyed on the host, e.g. WrapProductionSilentHookCommandForOS(cmd, agentpkg.HookHostIsWindows()) and WrapProductionPlainTextWarningHookCommandForOS(cmd, agentpkg.WarningFormatSingleLine, agentpkg.HookHostIsWindows()) — or better, pin both shapes deterministically with SetWindowsHookProbeForTesting(goos, probe) so the tests stop depending on the runtime OS at all. No droid test currently uses either the ForOS variants or that seam. ReplacesLegacyLocalDevHook needs the same treatment at its seeding step, which looks up the installed command before rewriting it.

For your triage question — "fix did not work" vs "second Windows defect behind the first": on the free evidence, the hook-delivery defect is fixed. The wrapper reaches entire and produces a real lifecycle event under both of droid's shell compositions. I have not exercised commit→checkpoint end-to-end (that needs the paid test or a synthetic droid transcript), so I can't rule out a further defect downstream of hook delivery; I can rule out the hook-delivery cause you diagnosed.

Nothing committed, nothing pushed, repo clean, temp worktree removed. All artifacts are in my scratchpad. Tell me if you want the synthetic full-lifecycle run (session-start → user-prompt-submit → stop → commit, with a fabricated droid transcript) — that would close the checkpoint question without spending API budget, and I can do it on request.
</cross-session-message>

The Windows box verified the fix, and caught a real regression I introduced. Both are handled.

## Verified on real Windows (droid 0.215.1, ARM64)

The free check reproduced the CI signature exactly. With the old `sh` wrapper pasted at a cmd prompt: **exit 0, "The system cannot find the path specified.", and `.entire\logs` never even created** — `entire` never ran, silently, which is why droid never reported anything wrong. With the new cmd.exe wrapper: reaches hook dispatch, and with a payload logs a real `session-start` lifecycle event. All 8 installed hooks are cmd.exe forms, zero `sh -c '`.

Two things it found that I hadn't established:

- **`sh` is on PATH on that box** (Git Bash via scoop). So `UseWindowsProductionHooks`' probe would have succeeded there and kept the broken wrapper. My reason for not gating on the probe went from a code-reading to an empirical result.
- **Double-wrapping works.** Droid nests our stored string inside its own `%ComSpec% /d /s /c`. It tested both compositions (0.215.1's bare join and 0.178.0's `shell:` wrap) with a Go spawner setting `SysProcAttr.CmdLine` directly — a byte-exact model of `windowsVerbatimArguments`. Both log `session-start`. I had reasoned through cmd's `/S` quote-stripping but never tested it; now it's tested.

## The regression — mine, now fixed

Three pre-existing droid tests hardcoded the sh wrapper, so on a Windows host they asserted a command `InstallHooks` no longer writes: `FreshInstall`, `PreservesUserHooksOnSameType`, `ReplacesLegacyLocalDevHook`. It confirmed this against `main` on the same box — there they fail only with TempDir cleanup noise and **zero** assertion failures. CI would never have caught it: the Windows job runs `-run '(Windows|MSYS)'` and none of those names match. Only someone running the full suite on Windows sees it — i.e. you, on that box.

Fixed by routing them through `droidHookCommand` / `droidStopHookCommand`, which apply the same host-keyed selector the implementation uses, so no hardcoded form remains to drift. I took that over pinning the seam, because pinning would make them assert the sh form on Windows — a shape never installed there. Verified with a temporary scaffold that pinned the host to Windows: **18 assertion failures with the old helper, zero with the new**, then deleted the scaffold. Lint clean, all agent packages green, and the CI Windows filter still selects both new tests.

## Two things need you

**Your commit is blocked — 1Password signing has stopped responding.** `commit.gpgsign=true` with SSH format, and both attempts died on `error: 1Password: failed to fill whole buffer`. The regression fix is staged but uncommitted; the branch on origin still has only the first commit and therefore still carries those three red tests. Unlock 1Password and I'll commit and push immediately. I haven't touched your signing config.

**The paid e2e is still unrun** — `FACTORY_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` are both unset on that box, and it correctly declined to go hunting for credentials. Those are yours to supply if you want `TestMultiSessionSequential` run for real.

Meanwhile I've asked it to do the synthetic full-lifecycle run it offered (fabricated droid transcript through session-start → stop → commit). That costs nothing and closes the one question I couldn't answer earlier: whether anything is broken *downstream* of hook delivery. Hook delivery itself is now confirmed fixed.

drift. The two tests that assert WHICH wrapper is chosen keep naming it
outright — they pin the host with SetWindowsHookProbeForTesting, and reusing
the selector there would restate the implementation and pass either way.

## What the synthetic run showed

On real Windows ARM64: fabricated droid payloads fired through the commands Entire actually wrote into `.factory/settings.json`, read back with quotes intact and spawned through droid 0.215.1's real double-wrapped composition. HEAD came out carrying `Entire-Checkpoint: 01M238D0PXJAKPCAK74KS2DQBR`, and `explain` shows a complete checkpoint — intent, both modified files pulled from the tool_use blocks, 6.3k tokens matching the usage blocks, transcript intact.

The cleanest evidence is the log contrast against the CI artifact:

| | CI artifact (broken) | Windows box (fixed) |
|---|---|---|
| lifecycle events | none | session-start, turn-start, turn-end, session-end |
| prepare-commit-msg | "no active sessions" | "trailer added" |

Same log line, opposite value.

It also caught its own methodology error and told me: run 1 accidentally lost the outer quotes during extraction, so only run 2 is faithful. Both landed a checkpoint, but it reported run 2 as the result. That's the difference between evidence and a green tick.

Its read, which I agree with: hook delivery is fixed and Entire's whole downstream path works on Windows. But a second defect downstream is **unsupported, not excluded** — the payloads are faithful to `types.go` and `transcript.go`, not to a captured droid session, so a field real droid sends differently wouldn't surface. The subagent `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse[Task]` path is untested. The paid e2e is still what closes it.

content.text:
Reading that as the original defect — the thing this branch fixes:

**Factory Droid produced no checkpoints on Windows.** Commits landed normally, but Entire never recorded a session, so nothing was ever captured.

The cause was one line of shell mismatch. Entire writes droid's hook command as:

```
sh -c 'if ! command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then exit 0; fi; exec entire hooks factoryai-droid session-start'
```

Droid's **Windows** build hands every hook command to `cmd.exe` (its macOS/Linux build uses `sh`). cmd.exe reads that string's `>` as its own redirection and `&` as a command separator, so the line is shredded before any shell sees it — `entire` is never executed. It fails with **exit code 0**, which is why nothing anywhere reported a problem.

No hooks → no session → the commit hook has nothing to condense → no checkpoint.

The fix: droid now installs native cmd.exe wrappers whenever the host is Windows. Notably *not* gated on the existing `UseWindowsProductionHooks` probe, because that probe only tests `sh -c 'exit 0'` — a command with no cmd.exe metacharacters — so a machine with Git Bash reports "sh works" and keeps the broken wrapper. Verified empirically: the Windows box has `sh` on PATH and would have hit exactly that.

Two other things in this thread could also be called "broken", so if you meant one of them:

- **A regression I introduced** — three existing droid tests hardcoded the `sh` form and started failing on Windows. Fixed, verified on the Windows box (13 assertion failures → 0), staged locally.
- **Your 1Password SSH agent**, which is still down (`ssh-add -l` → "The agent has no identities"). That's the live blocker: the regression fix is unpushed, so `origin/fix-droid-ai-windows-test` still carries those three broken tests.

          # opencode by npm: its install script resolves its version through an
          # unauthenticated api.github.com call it gives no way to authenticate,
          # so it is rate-limited at random.
          npm install -g @openai/codex @github/copilot opencode-ai
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          echo "AGENTS=claude-code opencode codex cursor-cli factoryai-droid copilot-cli" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # cursor-cli is absent: its E2E driver sends every prompt through tmux
      # (e2e/agents/cursor_cli.go), because Cursor's headless -p mode fires no
      # hooks — and there is no tmux on Windows.
      - name: Install agent CLIs (Windows)
        if: matrix.os == 'windows-latest'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex
          npm install -g @openai/codex @github/copilot opencode-ai
          # Stop does not cover native commands ($PSNativeCommandUseError-

content.content:
name: Nightly Install Smoke

# Every other E2E workflow builds the CLI from source. This one installs the
# published nightly the way a user does and runs one smoke test per agent
# against it, on each OS.

on:
  schedule:
    # 3h after nightly.yml tags at 06:00, so release.yml has published.
    - cron: "0 9 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      test:
        description: "Test name filter (regex)"
        required: false
        # Keep in sync with the TEST_FILTER fallback below, which is what a
        # scheduled run uses.
        default: "TestMultiSessionSequential"

concurrency:
  group: nightly-install-smoke
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    # Above the sum of the agents' own retry ceilings (~85m: 9 + 18 + 13.5 +
    # 13.5 + 18 + 13.5, see the step caps below) plus setup, so the per-step cap
    # is always the one that binds — a step timeout leaves an attributable row
    # in the table, a job timeout kills Summarize and the artifact upload with
    # it. Legs measure 6m30s-8m40s; this only binds on a hang in one of the
    # uncapped setup steps.
    timeout-minutes: 90
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      # For copilot-cli. Permissions are job-wide, so the install steps see
      # this scope too — accepted: they install and run the binary every later
      # step executes with the agent keys and this token, so withholding it
      # there guards nothing. Public repo, so only the Copilot quota has value.
      copilot-requests: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
    env:
      # What a first-run `entire enable` writes (setup.go). Unset, the harness
      # pins legacy git-branch, which no fresh install has.
      E2E_CHECKPOINT_STORE: git-refs
      TEST_FILTER: ${{ github.event.inputs.test || 'TestMultiSessionSequential' }}
      # Not $PWD: under Git Bash that is /d/a/cli/cli, which the Go test binary
      # resolves against the current drive.
      ARTIFACT_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}/e2e/artifacts

    steps:
      # Install first, checkout second: the ref comes from the installed
      # binary's version. GITHUB_TOKEN because the installers resolve the tag
      # through the releases API, which 403s unauthenticated from a shared
      # runner IP (reported as "check your internet connection").
      - name: Install nightly CLI (Linux)
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Install nightly CLI (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos-latest'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          brew tap entireio/tap
          brew trust entireio/tap
          brew install --cask entire@nightly

      # The README's nightly invocation. The installer updates only the stored
      # user PATH, which later steps do not re-read, hence GITHUB_PATH.
      - name: Install nightly CLI (Windows)
        if: matrix.os == 'windows-latest'

if: matrix.os == 'windows-latest'
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          iex "& {$(irm https://entire.io/install.ps1)} -Channel nightly"
          "$HOME\.local\bin" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_PATH -Encoding utf8 -Append

      # Pin the checkout to the tag that produced the installed binary, so the
      # harness and the CLI under test come from one commit.
      - name: Resolve nightly tag and binary path (Unix)
        if: matrix.os != 'windows-latest'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version_line=$(entire version | head -1)
          echo "$version_line"
          tag="v$(echo "$version_line" | awk '{print $3}')"
          # Fail closed: a stable or unparseable version means the install
          # resolved the wrong channel.
          case "$tag" in
            v*-nightly.*) ;;
            *) echo "expected a v*-nightly.* version, got '$tag'" >&2; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          {
            echo "NIGHTLY_TAG=$tag"
            echo "E2E_ENTIRE_BIN=$(command -v entire)"
          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Resolve nightly tag and binary path (Windows)
        if: matrix.os == 'windows-latest'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          # Stop is what makes the Write-Error below terminating. The runner
          # prepends it too, but this step depends on it, so it says so.
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $versionLine = (entire version | Select-Object -First 1)
          Write-Host $versionLine
          $tag = "v$($versionLine.Split(' ')[2])"
          # Fail closed: a stable or unparseable version means the install
          # resolved the wrong channel.
          if ($tag -notlike "v*-nightly.*") {
            Write-Error "expected a v*-nightly.* version, got '$tag'"
          }
          "NIGHTLY_TAG=$tag" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Encoding utf8 -Append
          "E2E_ENTIRE_BIN=$((Get-Command entire).Source)" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Encoding utf8 -Append

        with:
          ref: ${{ env.NIGHTLY_TAG }}
          # An agent process runs in this checkout; keep the token out of
          # .git/config.
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup mise
        uses: jdx/mise-action@f10502fc09dadecfefb962fff68ce77213930204 # v4

content.text:
I've prepared the edit, but hit a blocker and — more importantly — found that this workflow **cannot validate the fix**.

## The workflow tests the published nightly, not your branch

Its own header says it: *"Every other E2E workflow builds the CLI from source. This one installs the published nightly the way a user does."* It installs the nightly, reads `entire version` to derive `NIGHTLY_TAG`, then does `actions/checkout` with `ref: ${{ env.NIGHTLY_TAG }}` — **discarding whatever branch you dispatched from**.

So enabling droid there and dispatching it today would install the *pre-fix* nightly, fail exactly as before, and prove nothing. The re-enable is still the right change to make — it just validates on the first scheduled run *after* the fix ships:

1. fix merges to main → 2. `nightly.yml` tags 06:00, release publishes → 3. smoke at 09:00 installs it and runs droid on Windows

The 3-hour gap means the scheduled run is self-consistent. Only a manual dispatch before a post-fix nightly exists would give a misleading red.

## The edit, ready to apply

```diff
           irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex
+          irm https://app.factory.ai/cli/windows | iex
           npm install -g @openai/codex @github/copilot opencode-ai
-          # The iex line needs no such guard: that installer throws or exits on
-          # every failure path, and both end this step. Verified 2026-09-09.
+          # Neither iex line needs such a guard: both installers throw or exit
+          # on every failure path, and that ends this step. Verified 2026-09-09
+          # for claude, 2026-09-10 for droid, whose installer shadows
+          # Write-Error with one that exits 1.
           "$HOME\.local\bin" | Out-File ... GITHUB_PATH ...
+          # droid's Windows installer puts droid.exe in %USERPROFILE%\bin, not
+          # .local\bin, and updates only the stored user PATH, which later
+          # steps do not re-read.
+          "$HOME\bin" | Out-File ... GITHUB_PATH ...
-          "AGENTS=claude-code codex copilot-cli opencode" | ...
+          "AGENTS=claude-code codex copilot-cli opencode factoryai-droid" | ...
```

The `~\bin` detail is load-bearing and I verified it against the actual installer script: droid lands in `%USERPROFILE%\bin`, *not* the `.local\bin` the other agents use. Same source confirms its `Write-Error` shadow exits 1, so it needs no `$LASTEXITCODE` guard.

## Still blocked, and now it blocks more

I could not apply this in-tree. `nightly-e2e.yml` doesn't exist on my branch (25 commits behind main), so pulling main is a prerequisite — and rebase or merge both write a commit, which needs a signature. **1Password is still down** (`ssh-add -l` → "The agent has no identities"). So the workflow edit, the regression fix, and the rebase are all queued behind one unlock.

The patched file is at `scratchpad/wf/nightly-e2e.yml`; I'll apply it the moment I can rebase.

## If you want validation before merge

`e2e-windows.yml` **does** build from source on a Windows runner, but is hardcoded to claude-code (`go run ./e2e/bootstrap claude-code`, `--agent claude-code`). Adding an `agent` input would give a genuine pre-merge Windows check of this fix using the repo's own secrets. Want me to do that? It's a small change, it spends real API budget when dispatched, and it's the only path I can see that tests *your branch's code* on Windows.

git add .github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml && git commit -F - <<'EOF'
nightly-e2e: put factoryai-droid back on the Windows agent list

The exclusion was for the hook-path defect this branch fixes: droid's
Windows build runs hook commands through cmd.exe, which shredded the sh
wrapper, so no agent hook fired and no checkpoint was ever recorded.

Restoring takes the three things the exclusion comment named — the name in
AGENTS, the installer, and its bin directory on PATH. That directory is
%USERPROFILE%\bin, not the .local\bin the other Windows installers use;
droid's install.ps1 picks it and updates only the stored user PATH, which
later steps do not re-read.

The added iex needs no $LASTEXITCODE guard for the same reason the claude
one does not: droid's installer shadows Write-Error with a function that
exits 1, so every failure path ends the step.

Note this workflow installs the PUBLISHED nightly and checks out the tag it
resolves from `entire version`, so it does not test this branch. It first
exercises the fix on the scheduled run after a nightly carrying it ships —
tagging at 06:00 precedes the 09:00 smoke, so the two stay in step. A manual
dispatch before then would install a pre-fix nightly and fail.
